title: Blocking embroidery
subtitle: Stretching and pinning a washed embroidery to dry square and flat.
excerpt: Blocking restores the shape of embroidery that has been pulled off-grain by the tension of stitching or hoop use. The damp piece is stretched over a padded board, pinned square, and left to dry. Most distorted pieces come back straight with a single block.
sourceNotes: Blocking technique for needlework synthesised from contemporary practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of stretching a damp finished piece over a padded board and pinning it square, then leaving it to dry in that position. Blocking removes hoop distortion and corrects any off-grain pulling caused by stitching tension.

content.text: is done while the embroidery is still damp from washing. The fibres are pliable when wet and will dry in whatever shape they are pinned to. A piece that looks noticeably out of square usually comes back flat and true after a single block.

A blocking board is any firm, padded surface you can pin into: a foam board, a piece of thick cork board, or a dedicated blocking board with a grid. The grid lines make squaring easy. You need rustproof pins or stainless steel T-pins.
While the embroidery is still damp from washing, lay it face down on the blocking board.
Pin the centre of each side to the board, pulling the fabric gently to meet the grid line.
Working from the centres outward, pin along each side at 1 to 2 cm intervals. Pull the fabric gently straight; do not overstretch.
Check the corners are square and that the grain lines are straight.
Leave to dry completely, away from direct heat. Do not remove pins until the piece is fully dry, which may take several hours.

items.symptom: The piece still looks off-grain after drying
items.cause: The pins were removed before the piece was completely dry.
items.fix: Dampen the piece again, re-pin, and leave for longer. The piece must be bone dry before unpinning.

items.symptom: Rust marks appear where the pins were
items.fix: Always use stainless steel or rustproof T-pins. Remove standard steel pins immediately after drying.
